messages:
alex kim: Quick thought from intake: we should codify who owns what for pre-serve checks. Proposal: infra takes runtime safety & perf smokes; ML owns evaluative benchmarks and golden corpora. Trying to avoid duplicate fullbench runs.

maya singh: Sounds reasonable. Can we define exactly which signals travel across the registry -> runtime boundary? Tokenizer version, seqlen, perf hints, and a small quality whitelist?

sergey petrov: From infra POV, we need lightweight checks that catch quantization regressions. Suggest a tiny ensemble smoke: fp16 and int8 shadow on a 500-sample golden subset. Keep it under 10m per job.

nina r.: Also need artifact ACLs and provenance. Right now bench-bucket access is manual. Registry manifest should include storage path + signed artifact SHA + KMS id.

maya singh: Example (minimal) manifest line: ```
{"model_id":"m-2026-0715","tokenizer":"spm_v3","tokenizer_hash":"tknhash123","seqlen":4096,"artifact_sha":"sha256:deadbeef","eval_set":"gold_small","thresholds":["ppl_delta<0.15","top1_exact>0.92"]}
```

build-bot: Manifest publish OK: registry:/models/m-2026-0715/manifest@sha256:deadbeef. CI job queued for smoke. https://reg.internal/m/m-2026-0715

alex kim: Good. Another runtime idea: runtime exposes a compact header "x-compat" with three comma-separated scores: tok_match, kv_ok (t/f), perf_risk (low/med/high). This keeps gates simple.

jordan: If we use categorical perf_risk we avoid constant floating thresholds. But automation prefers numeric. Maybe both: header + numeric compat_score 0..100 for rollouts.

maya singh: ML will publish thresholds in manifest. Automations can map numeric score to rollout policy. Keep mapping deterministic.

sergey petrov: Operational flow I'd like: 1) registry ingest + manifest validation, 2) infra ensemble smoke (shadow fp16/int8 on n=500), 3) generate compat metrics, 4) ML sampled bench (n=2k) async, 5) promote to canary if compat passes. Full bench is optional pre-GA.

nina r.: Add: enforced canary automatic rollback if error rate or latency p95 regresses > set limit. Ops should own runbook.

ops-liz: I can wire automatic rollback to rollout-service, but we need a single signal to subscribe to. Suggest compat_score + error_rate. We'll wire both.

alex kim: Action items: maya + nina: finalize manifest schema and ACL/KMS fields by Wed. sergey + infra: deliver ensemble-smoke prototype (500 samples) by next Tue. jordan + ops: rollout hooks for compat_score + rollback by EOW.

jordan: I'll create the rollout board tickets and add a sequence diagram.

maya singh: Note for governance: ML decides quality thresholds; infra enforces runtime safety. We'll record owners in manifest metadata.

sergey petrov: Repro tip: make sure manifest includes deterministic seed and tokenizer hash so ML bench runs are replayable. I'll add `repro_seed` and `tokenizer_hash`.

nina r.: For private corp models include allowed_orgs list and kms_key_id in manifest. I'll add to the schema doc.

build-bot: Reminder: intake sync Friday 11:00 to review prototype. Attendees: alex kim, maya singh, sergey petrov, nina r., jordan, ops-liz.

alex kim: I'll draft a short RFC after the sync outlining ownership and the manifest contract. Post any objections here before I publish.

maya singh: No objections. Will start a PR for the manifest proto after the meeting.

ops-liz: We'll also add a brief canary checklist to ops-runbooks (alerts, rollback steps).

alex kim: Great, thanks everyone. End of thread.
